tool.name: scDblFinder
tool.description: detect doublets in single-cell RNA-seq data

configfiles.configfile:
files <- list( matrix = '$input_matrix', genes = '$input_genes', barcodes = '$input_barcodes', table = '$table' ) #if str($clusters.mode) == 'file': files[["clusters"]] <- '$clusters.clusters_file' #end if #if $samples.use == 'yes': files[["samples"]] <- '$samples.samples_file' #end if #if $output_singlets: files[["out_dir"]] <- '@TXOUT@' #end if
params <- list( clusters_mode = '$clusters.mode', labels_header = $labels_header, dbr_per1k = $advanced.dbr_per1k, nfeatures = as.integer($advanced.nfeatures), dims = as.integer($advanced.dims) ) #if $samples.use == 'yes': params[["multi_sample_mode"]] <- '$samples.multi_sample_mode' #end if #if str($advanced.dbr) not in ('', 'None'): params[["dbr"]] <- $advanced.dbr #end if #if str($advanced.dbr_sd) not in ('', 'None'): params[["dbr_sd"]] <- $advanced.dbr_sd #end if
seed.val <- as.integer($advanced.seed)

param.name: input_matrix
param.label: Count matrix
param.help: Raw (not normalized) UMI counts in Matrix Market format, genes as rows and barcodes as columns, e.g. the filtered matrix.mtx from Cell Ranger, STARsolo or DropletUtils.

param.name: input_genes
param.label: Genes
param.help: genes.tsv or features.tsv. The first column is used as the gene identifier.

param.name: input_barcodes
param.label: Barcodes
param.help: barcodes.tsv, one barcode per line, in the same order as the matrix columns. Use called cells only, not all droplets.

param.name: mode
param.label: Generate artificial doublets
param.help: How scDblFinder creates the artificial doublets it learns from.
param.option: Random: combine random pairs of cells
Cluster-based: cluster the cells first and combine cells from different clusters
Cluster-based, using my own cluster labels

param.name: clusters_file
param.label: Cluster labels
param.help: Two columns: barcode and cluster. Every barcode must have a label.

param.name: use
param.label: Matrix contains several samples or captures
param.help: Doublets only form within one capture, so samples should be processed separately.

param.name: samples_file
param.label: Sample labels
param.help: Two columns: barcode and sample (or capture). Every barcode must have a label.

param.name: multi_sample_mode
param.label: Multi-sample mode
param.option: singleModel: one model for all samples
singleModelSplitThres: one model, thresholds set per sample
asOne: treat all samples as one (only if they are not separate captures)

param.name: labels_header
param.label: Label files have a header line
param.help: Applies to the cluster and sample label files.

param.name: output_singlets
param.label: Output a count matrix with doublets removed
param.help: Writes matrix.mtx, genes.tsv and barcodes.tsv for the singlets only.

param.name: dbr
param.label: Expected doublet rate
param.help: Leave empty to estimate it from the number of cells (see the next option).

param.name: dbr_per1k
param.label: Expected doublet rate per 1000 cells
param.help: Used when the expected doublet rate is empty: the rate is this value times the number of cells divided by 1000. The default (0.8% per 1000 cells) is suited to 10x Chromium.

param.name: dbr_sd
param.label: Uncertainty of the expected doublet rate
param.help: Standard deviation of the doublet rate. Leave empty for the default (40% of the rate).

param.name: nfeatures
param.label: Number of top features to use

param.name: dims
param.label: Number of principal components to use

tool.help:
**What it does**
scDblFinder_ finds *doublets*: droplets that captured two cells instead of one. Doublets look like cells with mixed or unusually high expression and can appear as false intermediate states or small spurious clusters.
The tool creates artificial doublets by combining real cells, then trains a classifier (gradient-boosted trees) to tell them apart from the real cells, using features such as the density of artificial doublets among each cell's neighbours. Every barcode receives a doublet score and a call (``singlet`` or ``doublet``), with the threshold set from the expected doublet rate.
.. _scDblFinder: https://bioconductor.org/packages/scDblFinder
-----
**Input**
A count matrix of **called cells** in 10x layout (``matrix.mtx``, ``genes.tsv`` or ``features.tsv``, ``barcodes.tsv``), for example the *filtered* output of Cell Ranger, STARsolo or DropletUtils. Use raw counts, not normalized values. Empty droplets should already be removed, but run it before strict quality filtering, since removing cells changes the expected doublet rate.
Optional label files are tab-separated with two columns, barcode and label::
barcode cluster AAACCTGA... 3 AAACCTGC... 1
- **Cluster labels**: cluster-based artificial doublets work best when the data has distinct cell types. Without labels you can let the tool cluster the cells, or use random pairs. - **Sample labels**: if the matrix combines several captures, give each barcode its capture so doublets are only simulated within a capture.
**Expected doublet rate**
By default the rate is estimated from the number of cells (0.8% per 1000 cells, suited to 10x Chromium). Set it explicitly if your platform or loading differs.
-----
**Output**
- **Doublet calls**: one row per barcode with ``class`` (singlet or doublet), ``score`` (0 to 1), and the cluster and sample used, if any. - **Singlets matrix** (optional): the input matrix restricted to the singlets, in the same 10x layout.
The number of doublets and singlets called is printed in the tool's standard output.
